  <p class="lead">880-930 AD</p>
  </div>
  <div class="tab-pane fade" id="nav-aryaksemisvara-life" role="tabpanel">
  Āryakṣemīśvara was a prominent Indian philosopher and poet who lived in the 9th and 10th centuries CE. While his exact date of birth and death are uncertain, scholars believe that he lived in Kanauj. He was born around 880 CE and passed away around 930 CE. He has made a mention that he was patron by the King Mahipāladeva. Apart from that, very little is known about Āryakṣemīśvara's life, but he is primarily known for his work on Advaita Vēdānta philosophy, particularly his magnum opus, the Jñānasiddhi. The Jñānasiddhi is a highly regarded work in the Advaita Vēdānta tradition, and is considered one of the most important texts on the topic. In addition to the Jñānasiddhi, Āryakṣemīśvara is also believed to have authored other works on Advaita Vēdānta, although their authorship is not entirely certain. Apart from his philosophical works, Āryakṣemīśvara is also known for his contributions to Sanskrit literature, particularly in the fields of poetry and drama. He is believed to have written several Sanskrit plays, although only a few of these works have survived to the present day. Some sources also attribute Caṇḍakauśika and Naiṣadhānanda Kāvya’s to Āryakṣemīśvara. He is remembered as a significant figure in Indian philosophy and literature, particularly for his contributions to the Advaita Vēdānta tradition.
  </div>
  <div class="tab-pane fade" id="nav-aryaksemisvara-contribution" role="tabpanel">
  Āryakṣemīśvara was a notable figure in the field of Sanskrit literature during the 12th century. He contributed immensely to various genres of Sanskrit literature, such as drama, poetry, and philosophy. His works are known for their intricate language, rich cultural references, and deep philosophical insights. He is renowned for his plays, especially &quot;Caṇḍakauśika,&quot; which is a masterpiece of Indian drama. He also wrote &quot;Naiṣadhānanda Kāvya,&quot; which is a romantic epic poem that portrays the story of Nala and Damayanti. His philosophical treatise, &quot;Jñānasiddhi,&quot; is a significant contribution to Advaita Vēdānta, and it discusses the nature of the self and the ultimate reality. Overall, Āryakṣemīśvara's contributions to Sanskrit literature have greatly enriched Indian culture and continue to inspire scholars and enthusiasts alike.
  </div>
